note: INTERNAL troubleshooting corpus — factory fault/error codes with meaning + likely causes + the confirming test. Powers Ann's diagnose tool + the tech app 🧠 button. Part numbers are intentionally omitted — they come from the live Marcone/Amazon lookup + this shop's TDR history, never guessed. Samsung shows the SAME fault as '__E' on older displays and '__C' on newer (C = Check); both forms are stored so a tech's exact typing always resolves. For board-variant families (GE/LG ranges) the meaning says to confirm against the model tech sheet.

codes.test: Check lid-lock coil continuity + connector; cycle lock manually.
Inspect lock mechanism + striker alignment.

codes.meaning: Long drain — water not draining fast enough
codes.test: Check pump filter for debris; verify pump runs + ohms within spec.

codes.meaning: Long fill / low water (LF) — not enough water entering
codes.test: Verify both supply valves open + screens clear; check inlet valve ohms.
Run rinse/drain; advise HE detergent; confirm drain path clear.
Redistribute load; check suspension rods/struts.
Inspect rotor/stator + connector; check motor windings.

codes.meaning: Drain fault — water not out in time
codes.test: Clean pump filter; verify pump ohms + hose height per spec.
Ohm the lock solenoid + switch; check strike engages.
Power-cycle; manually release lock; check lock ohms.

codes.meaning: Overloaded — load too big/heavy to spin balanced
codes.test: Reduce/redistribute load; check suspension rods.
Reseat harnesses; confirm 120V to CCU; replace if faults persist.
Ohm the thermistor (~10k at room temp) + harness.
Check thermistor resistance + clear vent.
Clean sensor bars; short them to confirm sense; check harness.
Power-cycle 5 min; if it returns, replace main control.
Clean lint path + vent run; verify exhaust flow.
Confirm 240V both legs; check inlet connections.

codes.meaning: Low or no line voltage (one leg of 240V missing)
codes.test: Measure both legs at outlet (~120V each / 240V across).
Inspect touchpad ribbon + control board.
Verify fill + flow meter pulses.
Confirm supply + inlet valve ohms; free float.
Disconnect keypad ribbon — if fault clears, replace touchpad.

codes.meaning: Oven temp sensor (RTD) open or shorted
codes.test: Ohm the RTD sensor (~1080 ohm at room temp); check harness to control.
Check latch motor + switch continuity; free the latch.
Power-cycle 5 min; if it returns, replace the control.

codes.meaning: Power-outage alarm — temp rose during an outage (not a hardware fault)
codes.test: Acknowledge/clear the alarm; verify it's cooling now. Not a repair.
Open both valves; clean inlet screens; ohm the valve.

codes.meaning: Water supply error — not filling (older display)
codes.test: Open both valves; clean inlet screens; ohm the valve.
Clean front debris filter; verify pump operation.
Clean front debris filter; verify pump operation.
Level the machine; redistribute load; check suspension rods.
Level the machine; redistribute load; check suspension rods.
Inspect door lock switch continuity.
Inspect door lock switch continuity.
Inspect base for water; dry sensor; find leak source.
Inspect base for water; dry sensor; find leak source.
Check motor connector + hall sensor.

codes.meaning: Motor / hall sensor error (3C family — seen on all-in-one washer/dryer combos)
likely_causes: motor wiring / connector at motor and at the main/inverter PCB
codes.test: Power-cycle first (1-2 min) to clear a one-off. If it returns under spin: check the hall sensor + its connector, then the motor harness at both ends, then ohm the motor windings; PCB last. Confirm the exact sub-part against the model tech sheet.
Check motor connector + hall sensor.
Ohm the water temp sensor; check harness.
Confirm valve closes; check level sensor + pressure hose for clog/air.
Run rinse+spin; advise HE detergent; confirm drain path.
Free stuck button; if fault stays, replace control.
Ohm the wash heater + its thermistor.
Clear vent; ohm element + thermistor.
Clear vent; ohm element + thermistor.
Ohm the thermistor against spec; inspect harness for a short.
Ohm the thermistor; reseat/repair the connector.
Check door switch continuity.
Exit demo mode (hold Energy Saver + Fridge, or Freezer + Fridge, ~8s per the model).
Ohm the defrost/evap sensor on the fresh-food evap.
Ohm the defrost/evap sensor on the fresh-food evap.
Look for ice on the fan behind the back panel; spin fan; check motor + connector.
Look for ice on the fan behind the back panel; spin fan; check motor + connector.
Inspect the fresh-food evap fan for ice/obstruction; spin it; check motor ohms + connector.
Inspect the fresh-food evap fan for ice/obstruction; spin it; check motor ohms + connector.
Ohm the ice-pipe heater; verify the fill tube isn't frozen shut.
Ohm the ice-pipe heater; verify the fill tube isn't frozen shut.

codes.meaning: Ice maker function error — not making/ejecting ice (39E)
codes.test: Force a harvest in test mode; check the module motor + sensor; look for a frost-jam (our root-cause fix, not just a module swap).

codes.meaning: Ice maker function error — not making/ejecting ice (older display)
codes.test: Force a harvest in test mode; check the module motor + sensor; look for a frost-jam (our root-cause fix, not just a module swap).
Inspect the ice-room fan for ice/obstruction; spin it; check motor + connector.
Inspect the ice-room fan for ice/obstruction; spin it; check motor + connector.

codes.meaning: Display/power fault — needs a full power reset
codes.test: Unplug 5+ min; if it returns, reseat the display harness / check the main PCB.

likely_causes: ribbon/connector between display and main PCB
codes.test: Reseat the panel harness; check continuity; swap the suspect board.
Confirm supply + inlet valve.
Confirm supply + inlet valve.
Clean filter; verify drain pump; confirm disposal knockout removed.
Clean filter; verify drain pump; confirm disposal knockout removed.
Find/seal leak; dry the base leak sensor.
Find/seal leak; dry the base leak sensor.
Check the pump ohms + connector; confirm water level sensor.
Check the diverter motor + its microswitch/position.
Ohm the heater + thermistor; check for a thermostat trip.
Confirm valve closes; check the level sensor + float.
Free the stuck button; if it stays, replace the panel.
Open valves; clean inlet screens; check valve + pressure sensor hose.
Clean pump filter; verify drain pump runs.
Level unit; redistribute; check dampers.
Check door lock switch continuity.

codes.meaning: Motor locked / overload (often bearing or hall sensor)
codes.test: Check hall sensor + rotor; spin drum by hand.
Check inlet valve closes; verify pressure sensor.
Ohm temp sensor.
Clear vent; ohm the heater + thermistor.
Check the pressure sensor hose for clog/air; ohm the sensor.
Spin the drum by hand for drag; check motor + inverter board.

codes.meaning: Child lock is ON (NOT a fault)
codes.test: Hold the child-lock buttons ~3s to turn it off.
Clean full vent run; recheck.
Clear vent; inspect blower wheel.
Clear the entire vent run to the wall cap; inspect blower.
Ohm the thermistor.
Check the door switch continuity + latch strike.
Measure both legs at the outlet (~120V each / 240V across).
Confirm supply + inlet valve.
Verify drain pump + clear clog.
Check circulation motor.
Find leak; dry base/float.
Confirm the inlet valve closes; check the float + level sensor.
Ohm the thermistor; check the heater.
Check the freezer evap fan for ice/obstruction; spin it; ohm the motor.
Check the fresh-food fan for ice/obstruction; spin it; ohm the motor.
Ohm the defrost heater + thermal fuse/bi-metal; force a defrost in test mode.
Ohm the freezer sensor against the LG resistance chart.
Ohm the fridge sensor against the LG resistance chart.
Ohm the defrost sensor on the evaporator.
Check the ice compartment fan for ice; spin it; ohm the motor.
Clear the condenser area; spin the fan; ohm the motor.

likely_causes: harness between display and main board
codes.test: Reseat the comms harness; check continuity; swap the suspect board.

codes.meaning: Ice maker (craft/round ice) error — not making ice
codes.test: Run the ice maker test cycle; confirm fill + eject; ohm the ice maker sensor.

codes.meaning: Oven not heating / not reaching temp
codes.test: Confirm element/igniter draws; check the control relay + oven sensor. Confirm against the model tech sheet.

codes.meaning: Oven temp sensor open/short (varies by model — read the legend)
codes.test: Ohm the oven sensor; check the harness. Confirm the exact meaning on the model tech sheet.
Check the lock motor + switches; free the latch.
Open valves; clean screens; check valve.

codes.meaning: Fill time too long (didn't reach level in time)
codes.test: Check supply pressure + inlet screens; ohm the valve.

codes.meaning: Water leak or suds detected in the tub/base
codes.test: Find the leak; run a rinse to clear suds; advise HE detergent.
Clean pump filter; verify drain pump.
Clean the filter; verify the pump ohms + free flow.
Check door lock assembly.
Ohm the element.
Inspect keypad.
Check the evap fan motor + its connector; look for ice on the fan.
Reseat the board harnesses; check continuity; swap the suspect board.

codes.meaning: High-temperature alarm (fridge or freezer too warm)
codes.test: Confirm doors sealing; verify it's actually cooling; check evap fan + defrost.
Ohm the affected sensor; inspect the harness.
Ohm the affected sensor; reseat/repair the connector.

codes.meaning: Water not filling / level too low (i10)
codes.test: Confirm the supply faucet is open and the fill hose isn't kinked; check the inlet valve; free the float.
Clean the filter + sump; confirm the disposer knockout is removed; make sure the drain hose isn't pinched and is looped ≥32" from the floor; verify the drain pump.

codes.meaning: Water in the base pan — leak detected (i30)
likely_causes: leak into the base tripping the float
codes.test: Dry the base pan; find + seal the leak (hoses, sump, door seal); reset the base float switch.
Clean the glass trap + filter, clear the drain line, then re-run.

codes.meaning: Water in base pan — leak protection (Aquastop) tripped
codes.test: Tip unit to drain base; dry float; find leak source.

codes.meaning: Unexpected water inflow / inlet valve leaking through
codes.test: Confirm the inlet valve fully closes with power off; check for weeping.
Check supply pressure; verify the flow meter reads correctly.
Clean filter + arms; confirm full fill; check the circulation pump.
Clean filter + sump.
Clean filter + check drain path/pump.

codes.meaning: Drain pump blocked or drain hose kinked
codes.test: Remove the pump cover; clear debris from the impeller; straighten the hose.
Check heat pump / element.

codes.meaning: Drain fault — didn't drain in time
codes.test: Clean the pump filter; verify the pump + free drain path.

codes.meaning: Aquastop / leak in the base tripped
codes.test: Dry the base; find/seal the leak; reset the aquastop float.
Clear drain path; verify pump.
Full drain inspection.
Confirm the fill level; check the flood float + look for a leak.
Ohm the heater + thermistor.
Disconnect the keypad ribbon — if the fault clears, replace the touchpad.
Check the oven sensor ohms; watch for a welded bake/broil relay; replace the control if the relay is stuck.
Ohm the RTD (~1080 ohm at room temp); check the harness.
Ohm the RTD; inspect the harness for a short.
Disconnect the membrane ribbon — if the fault clears, replace the panel.

codes.meaning: GE top-load codes vary by board (e.g. 'dE' door, 'oE' overflow) — read the board legend
codes.test: Pull the tech sheet for the exact code on this board. On newer GE, read it via SmartHQ factory diagnostics.

codes.meaning: Newer GE — read every stored code + run factory tests via SmartHQ before opening a panel
likely_causes: n/a — diagnostic path, not a fault
codes.test: Connect through GE SmartHQ service diagnostics to pull the stored error history and run the factory component tests. Our GE moat.
Reset first; if it returns, check the wash/circulation motor and the drain path.
Check the heating element + thermistor for continuity; usually a tech fix.
Clean the filters and clear the drain line/hose.
Power off 5 minutes to clear; if it returns, suspect the control board.

codes.meaning: Stuck touchpad key / membrane switch fault (Er)
codes.test: A stuck key triggers it; if no button is stuck, replace the touchpad/control panel.
Needs the control reprogrammed or replaced (tech).
Check the vent assembly and its wiring.

codes.meaning: Heating water / low temp (HO or Hd) — often normal
codes.test: Usually NORMAL — it's heating water (~1-2 min per degree). Run hot water at the sink first; if it never satisfies, check the heater.
Shut the door until the latch clicks; if it persists, check the door latch/switch.
Press START/CANCEL to clear and restart; if it recurs, verify voltage + connections.

codes.meaning: Control lock is ON (LOC) — not a fault
codes.test: Hold the lock button ~3 seconds to toggle it off.

codes.meaning: Water-level (pressure) sensor signal out of range — control can't read the water level
likely_causes: clogged or kinked pressure hose / air-dome tube
codes.test: Clear the clear pressure hose of soap sludge/kinks and reseat both ends; reseat the sensor connector; ohm the sensor per the tech sheet. On front-load MHW models this is the F03 E01.

codes.meaning: Incoming water-temperature sensor (NTC) out of range
codes.test: Ohm the temperature thermistor cold vs spec; reseat its connector.

codes.meaning: Inlet water flow-meter / turbidity or flow sensor fault
codes.test: Check the flow-meter/turbidity sensor connector and ohm per tech sheet.

codes.meaning: Lid switch not sensed (control never sees the lid state)
codes.test: Ohm the lid switch open/closed; confirm the strike engages it.
Run the dispenser in diagnostics; check the actuator and connector.
Advise HE detergent only; run a clean cycle; verify drain flow.
Run the actuator in service mode; ohm the actuator; check for a slipping basket.
Replace/free the UI; confirm no button held in.
Reseat the communication harness; swap the suspect board per tech sheet.

codes.meaning: No water detected entering the tub (or pressure switch trip not sensed) — same as FH
likely_causes: water faucets not fully open / kinked fill hoses
clogged/kinked pressure (air-dome) hose or pressure switch
drain hose pushed too far down (siphoning)
codes.test: Open both faucets fully, unkink hoses; clean the inlet-valve screens; clear the pressure hose; ohm the valve coils; confirm the drain hose isn't inserted >6".

codes.meaning: No water / insufficient water detected entering the machine (Duet, = F20)
codes.test: Same as F20: verify supply + screens + inlet valve + pressure hose.

codes.meaning: Long drain — water not pumped out in the allotted time
codes.test: Clean the coin trap/pump filter; check the drain hose and standpipe; ohm the drain pump.
Ohm the NTC cold vs spec; reseat its connector.

codes.meaning: Serial communication error — CCU cannot talk to the motor control (MCU)
codes.test: Reseat the CCU↔MCU harness; check for power to the MCU; swap per tech sheet.
Run the dispenser in diagnostics; check the actuator.
Inspect the MCU for damage; ohm the motor windings; reseat connectors.
Check the pump and pressure-sensor circuits per tech sheet.

codes.meaning: Excessive suds detected — cycle paused to dissipate
codes.test: Use HE detergent only; verify drain flow; run a clean cycle.

codes.meaning: Drive-motor tachometer error — MCU can't read motor speed
codes.test: Check the tach/hall sensor and motor harness; spin the basket by hand for drag.
Ohm the heater element; check the relay/heater circuit.
Check the pressure hose/switch; verify the inlet valve fully closes.
Reseat harness; verify MCU power.

codes.meaning: Inlet/outlet thermistor resistance out of range
codes.test: Ohm the thermistor cold vs spec; clean the vent; reseat the connector.

codes.meaning: Restricted airflow / exhaust or gas-ignition timing fault
codes.test: Clean the full vent run; on gas, check igniter glow and valve coils.
Ohm the RTD (~1080–1100Ω at room temp); inspect wiring for a short.
Run the latch in diagnostics; check the latch switches.
Reseat the ribbon/harness; swap the suspect board.

codes.meaning: No water detected entering the dishwasher
codes.test: Confirm supply; check the fill valve and flow meter; free the float.
Check inlet valve flow and screen; verify supply pressure.

codes.meaning: Long fill / heater or diverter fault
codes.test: Check fill/flow, heater continuity, and diverter operation per tech sheet.

codes.meaning: Freezer evaporator fan not running normally (short form of Er FF)
codes.test: Pull the freezer evap cover — if iced, diagnose the defrost circuit (heater/sensor/thermostat); else spin/ohm the fan motor.

codes.meaning: Refrigerator (fresh-food) evaporator fan not running normally (Er rF)
codes.test: Check the fresh-food evap fan for ice/obstruction; ohm the motor.

codes.meaning: Condenser fan not running normally (Er CF)
codes.test: Clear the condenser area; spin and ohm the condenser fan motor.
Check the ice-room fan for frost/obstruction; ohm the motor.

codes.meaning: Defrost fault — defrost not completing (Er dH)
codes.test: Ohm the defrost heater and defrost thermistor; check the bi-metal for continuity cold.

codes.meaning: Water-flow sensor fault to the ice maker (Er gF)
codes.test: Confirm water supply/pressure; check the flow sensor and inlet valve.

codes.meaning: Freezer temperature sensor fault (short form of Er FS)
codes.test: Ohm the freezer thermistor vs spec; reseat the connector.
Ohm the fresh-food thermistor vs spec; reseat the connector.
Inspect the ice-room fan for frost; ohm the motor.
Ohm the ice-maker sensor; check the ice-maker harness.
Verify supply and flow sensor operation.

codes.meaning: Power failure occurred during the cycle
codes.test: Press start to resume; check for loose power/inlet connections.
Use HE detergent only; verify the drain and pump filter.

codes.meaning: Door will not lock (door open error)
codes.test: Confirm the door shuts fully; ohm the door lock; reseat the connector.
Check the lock switch circuit per service manual.

codes.meaning: Cool-down indicator (not a fault) — end-of-cycle tumble
codes.test: Informational; no repair unless it never clears.
Ohm the exhaust thermistor; clean the vent run.
Ohm the inlet thermistor; check the heater circuit.
Ohm the heater; check the relay on the main PCB.
Reseat the communication harness; swap the suspect board.
Find and dry the leak; the sensor won't reset until dry.

codes.meaning: Control lock is ON (not a fault)
codes.test: Hold the lock button ~3s to disable; informational only.

codes.meaning: Water not filling — no/low fill detected
codes.test: Open both faucets; clean the inlet screens; ohm the valve coils.
Clear the pressure hose; check the sensor connector.
Reseat the communication harness; swap the suspect board.
Confirm the unit is level; check the MEMS sensor per manual.
Ohm the door switch; confirm the door latches.
Ohm the thermistor; clean the vent run.

codes.meaning: Low water level in the sump
codes.test: Check fill valve and for leaks; verify the level sensor.
Free/replace the button board; confirm no key held.
Ohm the thermistor; reseat the connector.
Reseat the touchpad ribbon; if it returns, replace the EOC/control.
Run the latch; check the latch switches and wiring.
Verify the latch feedback; swap the control per service data.
Check the fill valve and flow meter; verify supply.
Find and dry the leak; sensor resets when dry.
Ohm the drain pump; check the pump relay/circuit.

codes.meaning: Door will not lock (control senses door open)
codes.test: Confirm the door shuts; ohm the door lock.
Cycle the lock; inspect for a bound latch.
Inspect the motor control board; ohm the motor.
Check the lock feedback to the motor control board.
Spin the basket for drag; check bearings; test the motor/control.
Ohm the thermistor; reseat the connector.
Check the heater relay and element continuity.

codes.meaning: Control / relay fault on the main board
codes.test: Power-reset; if it returns, service the control board.
Check the motor and heater relay per service data.
Verify supply and the flow meter signal.
Clean the filter; ohm the drain pump.
Confirm the door shuts; check the door lock.
Open the faucet; clean the inlet screen; check the valve.
Check the motor and control board per service data.

codes.meaning: Touchpad/control ribbon shorted or a key stuck (also shows as 5E on some models)
likely_causes: ribbon cable from touchpad to control shorted or moisture-damaged
codes.test: Unplug 5 min. If SE/5E returns, inspect the touchpad ribbon connector at the control for corrosion/moisture; a shorted touchpad or ribbon is the usual fix.

codes.meaning: Oven temperature sensor open or shorted
codes.test: Check the oven sensor resistance (~1080-1090 ohms at room temp for most Samsung ovens) and its connector; out-of-range or open reads = replace the sensor.

codes.meaning: Door lock stuck — the self-clean lock did not release
codes.test: Let the oven fully cool, then unplug 5 min to reset the lock cycle. If the door stays locked or C-d0 stays, the lock motor/assembly is the fix.

codes.meaning: Runaway temperature — the control shut the oven off for safety (it read a too-high or out-of-range temp)
codes.test: Unplug 5 min. If F10 returns, check the oven sensor resistance (~1080 ohms at room temp); a drifted sensor is the common cause, a stuck control relay the next.
With the oven cool, check the sensor resistance and its plug at the back; an open reading or unplugged connector = reseat or replace the sensor.
Check the oven sensor resistance and wiring for a short to ground; a shorted sensor or pinched wire is the fix.

codes.meaning: Oven door lock fault — the self-clean lock motor did not reach its locked/unlocked position
likely_causes: door lock motor/assembly jammed or failed
codes.test: Let the oven fully cool, then unplug 5 min. If the door stays locked or E011 returns, the door lock motor/assembly is the usual fix.

codes.meaning: Oven temperature sensor (NTC) fault — reads open or shorted
codes.test: With the oven cool, check the NTC sensor resistance and its connector; an open/shorted or out-of-range reading = replace the sensor.

codes.meaning: A control-panel key is stuck or the touch control reads a constant press
codes.test: Unplug 5 min and wipe the control panel dry. If E305 returns, a stuck key or the touch control board is the fix.

codes.meaning: Touchpad/control ribbon shorted or a stuck key (also shows as 5E) — the microwave controls lock up
likely_causes: touchpad ribbon cable shorted (often from steam/moisture)
codes.test: Unplug 5 min. If SE/5E returns, the touchpad ribbon or membrane is shorting — a tech reseats or replaces the touchpad. Do NOT open the cabinet; the microwave capacitor holds a dangerous charge.

codes.meaning: Defrost sensor fault — the defrost sensor reads open or shorted, so the defrost system can't run correctly (also shows as 25E)
codes.test: Check the defrost sensor resistance and its connector; an open/shorted reading = replace the sensor. If frost is building on the evaporator, check the defrost heater too.

codes.meaning: Flow meter fault — the control is not getting a valid water-flow signal
likely_causes: low water supply / kinked fill line
codes.test: Confirm the house water supply is on and the fill line is not kinked, then a tech checks the flow meter and inlet valve.

codes.meaning: Temperature sensor (thermistor) error — the control reads an invalid water-temperature signal
codes.test: Check the thermistor resistance and its connector; an open/shorted or out-of-range reading = replace the sensor.

codes.meaning: Items detected in the tub during a Clean Washer cycle — remove the load and restart (not a fault)
likely_causes: laundry left in the drum during the self-clean cycle
codes.test: Empty the drum completely and restart the Clean Washer cycle with nothing inside; the code clears.

codes.meaning: Oven temperature sensor shorted (pairs with E-08 open)
codes.test: Check the oven sensor resistance and wiring for a short; out-of-range or shorted = replace the sensor.
